biography.plain_text: Emily Roebling Cadwalader was an American heiress and philanthropist associated with Trenton and Philadelphia. She and her sister inherited the estate of their father, Charles Gustavus Roebling, who led the family's steel wire and cable business. Her grandfather, John Augustus Roebling, designed the Brooklyn Bridge. She married Richard McCall Cadwalader Jr.

long_biography.plain_text:
Emily Roebling Cadwalader helped a group of Trenton women turn a social club into a district-nursing service. After identifying the need for a nurse, the committee raised money through entertainments and rented a small apartment for the work. The service eventually grew into the city's Orthopaedic Hospital, treating children affected by polio.

She and her husband also made their country home, Fairwold, available to the government for convalescing servicemen at the end of the First World War. The couple stayed at their Philadelphia townhouse, their principal residence, while the estate served men recovering from military service.
